observations.text: Re-review delta at commit a4241d7, tree clean. ARGV: git diff --name-only 5843ed2..HEAD; exit 0; stdout: the test-side delta I judge here is two files only - tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs, each reading the resume verdict through to_read() and skipped() instead of the former public fields (4 changed lines in all, no scenario, generator, assertion or message touched) - beside the acceptance record, which adopts two in-crate locators (docs/feature/fix-repos-read-across-resume/acceptance.md, two new Covers blocks, nothing removed) and carries the examination rows E1-E6 as met. Production in the same span: crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/{resume.rs,mod.rs} (Resume is now one disposition per position, read through accessors), crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs (a release build carries no scan-write seam state) and crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs. No support file changed, so the fault table and the restart step I judged last round are unchanged bytes.

Every affected check run again at a4241d7, because the resume verdict, its two readers and the store changed. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 11 passed in 6.21 s, the three resume properties and the six journeys named in the output. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_and_accounts_core; exit 0; 11 passed in 0.03 s, so the second method-read file still collects and still observes its own laws. ARGV: cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store; exit 0; review-domain 105+28+34+2 passed (0.43 s for the lib, which holds the adopted domain property), adapter-review-store 49 passed in 56.18 s plus 6 passed. ARGV: cargo xtask check-arch; exit 0; stdout check-arch: OK (30 workspace members), which is T1 and T2 own check over the changed crates. ARGV: cargo test -p xtask --test review_app_test_fault_guard; exit 0; 7 passed including the_real_tree_passes, so the fault names of the seam this oracle uses are still cfg-gated after the release-build change. ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins; exit 0; 39 passed. No proptest regression file remains; git status --porcelain empty.

The adopted domain locator is sound, adds an observation nothing else makes, and I saw it go red twice. crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/mod.rs::a_resume_keeps_as_read_exactly_the_rows_the_scan_already_read drives resume_plan, the declared SUT of L1, L2 and L3, over plans of 0 to 10 rows of four accounts and four imports with any status, any bio check and any listed sources, and asserts (a) already_read() equals the positions whose generated status is read - computed in the test from the generated plan alone, so the oracle is independent of the production answer - (b) that no taken-over position is read now, and (c) that kept() is exactly those positions as read plus every position read now or carried as planned, in plan order, strictly increasing and inside the plan. Mutation A, in crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs, PlanRowStatus::Read => Some(Disposition::AlreadyRead) became Some(Disposition::ToRead): ARGV: cargo test -p review-domain; exit 101; the property FAILED (left == right on the taken-over rows) with 104 passed, and ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 101; 7 of 11 failed, the two resume properties plus five journeys, each naming the repo read again. Mutation B, status_kept giving Disposition::Carried => None (a carried row dropped from the kept plan): ARGV: cargo test -p review-domain; exit 101; the property FAILED at kept in plan order, with its status, right [KeptRow { position: 0, status: Planned }], while ARGV: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume; exit 0; 11 passed. So the locator is not a duplicate: it alone catches a kept plan losing a carried row, which no journey and no acceptance property observes, because the view type PickedUp exposes only whether a kept row carries an earlier read. Both files restored with git checkout --; tree clean.

The adopted adapter locator is sound and falsifiable, and L4 keeps its third case elsewhere. crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs::a_plan_reads_back_with_the_statuses_it_was_written_with writes 1 to 10 rows of either source with any status through record_plan into a real in-memory store and asserts latest_plan returns the written vector unchanged and latest_scan repos_read equals the count of rows written read; the expected value is the written vector itself, so the read path is not its own oracle. It subsumes L4/F115 (read, planned, planned) and L4/F116 (all planned) as generated instances, and L4's third case, a plan written for a run the store no longer holds, stays bound to a_purge_between_scan_start_and_plan_write_leaves_no_rows (F117), so nothing of L4 is now unobserved. Mutation C, in the plan-row insert of crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs, row.status.as_str() became PlanRowStatus::Planned.as_str(): ARGV: cargo test -p adapter-review-store --lib a_plan_reads_back; exit 101; FAILED with minimal failing input statuses = [Read], left status Planned against right status Read. Restored; ARGV: cargo test -p adapter-review-store --lib a_plan_reads_back; exit 0; 1 passed in 2.52 s over its 256 cases, inside the 56.18 s adapter lib suite that the 300 s default ceiling already holds; no per-test cap of this design covers an adapter round trip over a real store, and nothing here sits at half of a stated budget, so no nine-run median evidence was collected.

Closure and ownership after the adoption. Every obligation the two new locators carry keeps an oracle-owned locator as well: L1/F101, L2/F107 and L3/F111 stay bound to the three properties of tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs, and L4/F115 and L4/F116 stay bound to its journeys, so no promise of P1 or P2 now rests only on bytes the crafter owns - the adoption adds a second, lower observation of a law, it does not move one out of the oracle. That matches what this feature already accepted for L6/F313, L6/F314 and L4/F117, which were bound to in-crate adapter tests in the accepted round before this one. The method-read change preserves the oracle's meaning: the one sut_picked_up binding still makes exactly one call into resume_plan and still maps the verdict onto the declared view types, and the red of mutation A at this commit shows the change cost the oracle none of its falsifying power. typesafe: unavailable - the client at ~/.claude/skills/nw-typesafe-system-one/scripts/jev_decide.py is present but TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment (printenv | grep -i -c TYPESAFE_API_KEY, stdout 0), so every judgment here is locally derived from the measured runs and the read bytes.

diagnostic: Accepted at a4241d7, no finding open. The delta is two oracle-side files reading the resume verdict through to_read() and skipped() instead of its former fields, and an acceptance record that adopts two in-crate locators. The read change is meaning-preserving and still falsifying: the suite is green (11 passed, 6.21 s; the core suite 11 passed) and under a resume mutation that stops a run taking over a read row, 7 of its 11 tests fail, each naming the repo read again, so nothing was lost by reading the verdict through methods. Both adopted locators are sound at the declared SUT of their law, derive their expected value independently of the read path, and I saw each go red myself and restored it: the domain property fails on the taken-over rows when a read row becomes to-read, and fails on the kept statuses when a carried row is dropped from the kept plan, which no journey and no acceptance property can observe, so it is a distinct observation and not a duplicate; the adapter round trip fails with minimal input [Read] when the plan writer always writes planned. The adoption weakens no ownership: L1/F101, L2/F107, L3/F111, L4/F115 and L4/F116 each keep their oracle-owned locator, so no promise of P1 or P2 rests only on crafter-owned bytes, as this feature already accepted for L6 and L4/F117. L4's third case stays bound to the purge test. Every affected check ran again at this commit and passed, check-arch included, the tree is clean and no proptest regression file remains. typesafe: unavailable (no API key in this environment). Nothing in this delta blocks craft or completion.
